correctness.rationale: A synchronous Poisson coupling and L2 Gaussian-exponential perpetuity establish unique stationarity for any fixed d and |a|<1. The radial Fourier product obeys Phi(bu)-Phi(u)=u² Phi(u), is superpolynomially integrable for b>0, and implies I_(d+2)=(b^(-d)-1) I_d. Its planar Frullani integral is exactly log(1/b). The even closed form follows inductively; an exact odd-dimensional recurrence and dominated convergence for the one-dimensional Fourier integral give the sharp coefficient π/2. Finite numerical quadrature corroborates 38 cases but does not establish the theorem.

value.rationale: The primary 2024 paper explicitly motivates higher-dimensional extension. The exact planar contact law permits direct inversion of contraction strength from a local stationary observable, while the d-to-d+2 identity gives an all-dimensional local concentration transfer rule without solving new PDEs. The parity-dependent sharp logarithmic/power hierarchy resolves the full near-complete-reset dimensional singularity, a natural geometry-driven classification rather than an arbitrary finite example.
